title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridors 1 and 6 Connector Road (Aktobe-Kandyagash) Reconstruction Project

description.narrative:
The proposed project will (i) reconstruct the 89-kilometer highway connecting Aktobe and Kandyagash, and (ii) strengthen the institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol.
The project is aligned with the following impact: more jobs created, and Kazakhstan integrated into the regional and global economic system. The project will have the following outcome: efficient, reliable, and safe movement of people and goods in West Kazakhstan increased. Output 1: Aktobe-Kandyagash highway reconstructed to category I standard. The project will upgrade the 89-km two-lane category II and III road to a four-lane category I road that will connect Aktobe to Kandyagash. The project will widen the road to the category I standard with climate-resilient features, construct roadside service areas with sanitary facilities especially for women, reconstruct all bridges, build two new bypasses of villages, and improve road safety.
Output 2: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened. This output will strengthen KazAvtoZhol's institutional capacity by providing equipment; staffing; and training on financial management, procurement, project management, gender, and social safeguards management. The training sessions will include a minimum of 30% participation by women.

Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: Environment and social safeguards unit (with 30% female staff) established Achievement: N Progress/Status: On 28 October 2023, KAZH submitted information on the status of safeguard management. The package contained information about the current set up and standard operating procedure being followed in managing safeguard aspects, description of staff responsibilities and interactions in dealing with social and environmental safeguards at project preparation and implementation stages, the list of training courses conducted in 2023. According to KAZH, the Department of Technical Policy and Control (DTPQC), which deals with preparation of feasibility studies of investment projects and DEDs, is responsible for the review and approval of land acquisition and resettlement plant (LARP), environmental impact assessment (EIA/IEA). The PMU staffed with a social and environment safeguards specialist and the branch office are responsible for implementation of the LARP/IEE/EIA, preparation of CAPs. The PMU reports to the Department of Road Network Development, which was further reorganized in 2024 to the Department of External Loans and the Department of Road Network managing state-financed projects. Additionally, three staff of KAZH Branch office in Aktobe are responsible for overseeing safeguard-related tasks, dealing with local executive bodies and KAZH head office on land acquisition and environment-related activities. According to KAZH, the Department of External Loans, currently composed of 11 staff will be further strengthened, including for safeguards, in anticipation of new projects with ADB, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Islamic Development Bank and World Bank. ADB strengthened the importance of ensuring consistency in dealing with safeguards both at processing and implementation stages, requiring closer interaction between the DTPQC and the Department of External Loans, including the PMU. KAZH will submit the plan of such strengthening measures for safeguards by 23 July 2024. The target for 30% female staff for the proposed unit is at risk per mission conducted in July 2024. safeguards set up was discussed during the last mission and KAZH has reconfirmed that PIUs have been transferred to the Department of External Loans, created to work on IFI loans, and OIU's social safeguards specialist Ms. Sara Iskakova is currently working as safeguards specialist in that Department. She has been assigned to continue working for ADB loan 3829-KAZ. The PIU arrangements for future projects have been also discussed for another ADB project in processing (Kyzylorda-Zhezkazgan) with KAZH confirmation that the Department of External Loans and KAZH Branch offices to be responsible for safeguards compliance starting from project processing to implementation to ensure consistency. Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: Implementation plan to improve KazAvtoZhol's financial position developed Achievement: Y Progress/Status: In April 2023, the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan approved the Company Development Plan for 2023-2032 (the Plan), which includes strengthening the financial stability of KAZH. There are similarities and overlaps between this sub-output and the Plan. KAZH has confirmed that the financial sustainability is ensured by (i) the Republican Budget funds earmarked for Trust Management Agreements signed with the Ministry of Finance (MOF), Ministry of Transportation, and KAZH to operate republican roads and repay IFI loans and (ii) tolls collected from 3,200 km of republican roads, with the plan to increase the network of toll roads to 7,000 km by the end of 2025. The tolls are used to pay the cost of routine repair and maintenance of toll roads on self-financed basis and make payments for the leasing of maintenance equipment. KAZH will send a note on planned measures to strengthen its financial sustainability by 15 August 2024. To review that KAZH financial sustainability is based on (i) state (republican) budget funding (100%) for road projects, including IFI loans which are repaid from the state budget; and (ii) revenues from the toll roads. No other revenues are envisaged. All KAZH borrowings are decided by the Government and government resolutions are issued on the provision of sovereign guarantees(s) for each IFI loan.
